lines: Me
Excuse me.
I finished my report to Teacher Asagi and left the principal's office.
After bowing, I straightened my back and let out a small sigh.
The smell of brine and rust was still clinging to my clothes. I had just finished delivering the cursed item we had hauled up from the depths of the sea.
Cursed items related to magic, taken out of Japan, were being smuggled into Southeast Asia.
I had been assigned the mission to recover them after they left Japanese waters and entered the sea, with Dutch's help.
Me
...Well then. I wonder how Dutch is doing.
I had been exposed to a long stream of curses while fighting the fish that had mutated into monsters under the influence of the cursed item.
Because of that, Dutch is undergoing tests to check if he has been affected by the cursed item.
Invisible poison is the worst kind. Hoping for the best, I headed to the examination room where Dutch was.
When I entered the room, Dutch had just finished his examination. He was straightening his clothes as he looked at me coming in.
Dutch
Oh, you're here. The exam is over. No effects from that cursed item or whatever it is.
Dutch
Even if they say that, I have no idea what the effects of a cursed item are supposed to be.
I looked at Linoa, who had conducted the examination, and she gave a small nod. It really seems like there are no problems.
The only injuries were bruises and scrapes from when the boat was blown away.
Dutch
However, the girl doing the exams told me something. She said, "If you're worried, go take a medicinal bath."
Me
A medicinal bath?
Dutch
Yeah. She said, "It's effective for bruises too, and if you're worried about the effects of the cursed item."
Dutch
I've heard a bit about traditional Eastern medicine, but does a medicinal bath work on "voodoo" too?
I nodded lightly. Cursed items aren't something one gets familiar with easily. It's no wonder Dutch is skeptical.
Me
Of course, it's not just a folk remedy as is.
Me
It has been researched to counter injuries, poisons, and curses caused by magic, so both the techniques and the materials are derived from magic or handled by those well-versed in it.
As incidents affecting the general public began to increase, Gosha reviewed their treatment methods.
Standard medical care often struggles to recover patients from the harmful effects of demons.
It was also discovered that treatments used for Taimanin could be harmful to ordinary people.
Me
It's the soaking type rather than the drinking type, so it puts less strain on the body. It has some effect on external wounds, but it's particularly effective for mental issues.
Linoa recommending the medicinal bath for something like "voodoo" likely also had the intention of seizing the opportunity to gather data.
Dutch
Huh... so basically?
As if seeing right through me, Dutch raised the corner of his mouth in a smirk.
Me
Think of it like soaking in a hot spring to relax. Since we're in Japan, you might as well enjoy it as a tourist.
Hearing my answer, Dutch let out a soft laugh and shrugged his shoulders.
Dutch
That's very Japanese of you. Washing away curses in the bath, huh. Okay, not bad.
Me
What shall we do? Should we start the medicinal bath right away? Or go to the rest room? Or should we look at the reward documents first?
Those documents were a collection of literature regarding demons, specially released with Igawa Asagi's permission. Normally, access is strictly prohibited; it is top-secret material.
Dutch
Documents. If there's no 'cure,' then 'prevention' is a matter of life and death. The bath can wait.
I felt a quiet intensity in Dutch's calm tone. He clearly valued this highly.
There was an aura of life and death emanating from a man who had survived countless battles.
Everything from the outside world was cut off beyond the door.
The room was serene, with lighting and air conditioning meticulously controlled in every corner, not just for the books. It felt as if time had stopped here.
Dutch
Not bad... The setup is good enough to brew fine wine. I like it.
Dutch stopped walking, taking in the room with a wide sweep of his gaze, and muttered.
Then he looked at me and—
Dutch
...I'm counting on you.
He said just that one thing.
Me
Leave it to me.
I was confident that I knew this place better than any student, and better than most of the faculty.
It was a source of immense pride and joy that he liked this place and entrusted it to me.
I selected records primarily focused on the demons and monsters that had frequently appeared in the human world.
In addition to the ones we had actually faced, I included information from both domestic and international sources that, when cross-referenced, suggested they were likely this specific demon.
Dutch
Dutch silently scanned the documents. The device in his hand steadily translated the handwritten text.
Light swept over the characters, converting them instantly. Without frowning at the translation results, he simply absorbed the information.
He was a man of intense focus. He didn't hold his breath too long, maintaining a steady rhythm. He was less like a reader and more like a craftsman scrutinizing raw materials.
The library remained as quiet as ever. Only the sound of pages turning disturbed the stillness.
I settled into my chair and glanced at the clock once. It had been about an hour.
I spoke up just as Dutch finished one booklet and reached for the next.
Me
How are the documents?
Dutch
The material itself isn't bad. In fact, it's high quality. But there's too much of it.
Me
We can look at the rest another time... if fate allows.
Dutch
Hah. Without this device, I wouldn't be able to read a word of it. That's the only thing that's a bit frustrating.
Translation accuracy has its limits. Nuances and the temperature between the lines don't always come through. Yet that was the extent of his dissatisfaction.
Me
About the translation... I think we should translate it so people can read it without a device and spread the word, don't you?
Dutch
Hm...
It wasn't just a casual question. It was a kind of negotiation, a probe, an exploration, and a sincere inquiry.
Dutch
So, Fuuma. What do you think?
Dutch's question rang out heavy and quiet. It was of the same nature as mine, but I felt he was using it to confirm his own thoughts.
I let out a brief breath before weaving my words. Not just to answer the question, but to turn it back, as intended.
Me
If humanity were to unite against the demons, knowledge should be shared. Translated, published, everything.
Me
But...
I stopped there.
Dutch looked up from the page and fixed his gaze on me.
Dutch
But?
Me
In reality, not everyone shares the same goal.
Me
Some want to stand above others, and some want to force others into submission.
Dutch
Above all, if you used that to do business, you could make a fortune beyond imagination. Nothing sells quite like weapons.
Me
Yes. For those people, information is... a powerful weapon, a commodity usable against the demons or against us.
Me
And if, truly...
Me
When everyone believes in the same "truth," and someone who is "different" appears... that person immediately becomes the enemy.
As I spoke, what rose in my mind was the violence in the name of truth, repeated so many times in the past.
Dutch kept his eyes on me, listening intently.
Me
The idea that sharing the same values leads to unity is an illusion. Being the same can also be a reason for exclusion.
Me
Lumping everything under the single word "demon" and treating it as the enemy is powerful for cohesion, easy to understand, and allows for fervor.
Me
But... once that fervor starts, it is not easy to stop. Someone will always want to find the next "demon."
Dutch
Hmph...
Dutch let out a small snort. What it meant.
It was hard to judge from the sound alone, but the fact that he was still looking at me suggested I had passed.
Me
That is why I believe it is better for me to keep this information exclusive.
As became clear both this time and last time, the demons are expanding into Southeast Asia.
It is not just the demons.
There are also those who deal in commodities different from the materials in this library, linking with the demons to harm people.
That is precisely why—
Me
...The reason Dutch wanted the materials wasn't to fight the demons or eliminate them. It was to understand them, right?
At my words, Dutch neither nodded nor denied. He simply lowered his gaze back to the book's pages.
He gently pinched the corner of the page with his fingertip and turned to the next one.
Dutch
...A bit chatty, like a missionary, but it wasn't bad.
Dutch
As the boss leading the squad, you have the necessary qualities.
He turned another page, taking in the information within the limited time.
Dutch
Artists spout nonsense about understanding each other even without a shared language, and philosophers scream like parrots—
Dutch
But humans are the ones who pull the trigger, making excuses about different colors or shapes, even when they can communicate.
I deeply agreed with those words. If someone like Dutch is on the front lines, maybe there is still hope for this world.
Dutch
Just because you were born in a different place.
The corner of Dutch's mouth curled into a sarcastic smile. Judging by the words alone, it sounded like a truly ridiculous story.
Dutch
If clients who don't care about color or shape are coming—
The sound of a page flipping cut in.
Dutch
It never hurts to learn a greeting that doesn't bring blood rain.
Dutch
It's the basics of business.
Dutch looked up and said that.
Of course, that applies to the demons too—
Dutch
...It seems we can continue working with one of the major players. That's today's harvest, I suppose.
Those words were also directed at me.
Me
Same for me.
Watching Dutch continue reading the materials, I lowered my gaze to the pages of my own book.
This is not friendship. Our interests simply align.
Next time we meet, we might be pointing blades and gun barrels at each other.
Both Dutch and I are aware of that. In fact, that is the premise of our relationship. But that is exactly why it has value.
Joining hands despite our different positions. I felt that was the most important way to be.
